segments.t: korTTY runs on KTPH000macOS, Windows and LinuxKTPH001. The recommended installation is a self-contained package from the KTPH002GitHub Releases pageKTPH003; these packages include the Java runtime needed by korTTY, so users do not need to install Java separately.

Each native asset name includes its processor architecture. Use KTPH000 or KTPH001 for a native ARM package where one is listed and KTPH002 for an Intel or AMD package; Windows is the exception described below.
Use the KTPH000 assets on Apple Silicon and the KTPH001 assets on an Intel Mac. The DMG provides the normal installation experience; the ZIP contains the complete portable KTPH002 bundle.

Use the KTPH000 assets on Intel/AMD PCs and on Windows on ARM, where Windows runs them through x64 emulation. korTTY detects that emulated Windows ARM combination at startup and uses JavaFX's software renderer because the emulated Direct3D pipeline can leave windows blank; native x64 systems retain hardware rendering. korTTY does not currently publish a native Windows ARM package because the pinned OpenJFX line has no Windows ARM natives. The MSI is the installer; the ZIP contains the complete portable application directory, including KTPH001 and its runtime. The executable inside that directory is not a stand-alone single-file application.

Use the package for your architecture and distribution: DEB for Debian/Ubuntu, RPM for RPM-based distributions, Pacman KTPH000 for Arch Linux, Pacman KTPH001 for Arch Linux ARM, or the ZIP/TAR archive for a portable installation. The archive contains a complete KTPH002 application-image directory; it is not a Linux KTPH003 file.
Some features call external programs only when you use them:
Local KTPH000 and KTPH001 in KTPH002, or a configured KTPH003 binary path
Local KTPH000 in KTPH001, or a path configured in KTPH002Tools → Video ManagerKTPH003

The base korTTY package deliberately contains neither model weights nor a native llama.cpp runtime. When you enable integrated local AI, verified runtime packages from the public KTPH002korTTY llama.cpp runtime channelKTPH003 are installed independently under KTPH000 and GGUF models are downloaded or imported under KTPH001 (or referenced from a path you choose). Each runtime index and package is checked against the public Ed25519 trust root pinned in the korTTY source. This keeps the normal SSH client installer small and lets llama.cpp receive compatible stable updates without replacing the whole application.

CUDA is not part of the first runtime matrix. Under KTPH000AI Manager KTPH002 Local AIKTPH001, choose the preferred runtime backend: Auto/CPU/Metal on macOS or Auto/CPU/Vulkan on Windows/Linux. On a first installation, Auto prefers Metal on macOS and falls back to CPU when no compatible Metal package is available; on Windows and Linux it prefers the portable CPU package and falls back to Vulkan only when CPU is unavailable. Updates keep the active backend when a compatible package exists. Starting a model configured for another supported GPU backend offers to install the matching signed package. Runtime and model downloads can be several gigabytes, so verify free disk space and available RAM/VRAM before installation.

After installing korTTY, open KTPH000AI KTPH010 AI Manager KTPH011 Local Models KTPH012 Setup assistantKTPH001. It reviews privacy, detects memory, recommends Text/Coding/embedding GGUF models, shows the repository license and exact size, verifies the immutable download, assigns roles, and runs a real local chat or embedding function test. If no runtime is active, accept the signed-runtime installation prompt, or choose KTPH002Install runtimeKTPH003 in the same tab before importing a GGUF. The Hub's context length remains visible, while new models start conservatively at 4,096 runtime tokens until you change KTPH004Configure KTPH013 Context sizeKTPH005. Official packages can refresh recommendations and prompt-family mappings from a separate signed catalog; a build without that catalog trust root stays fully usable with its offline bootstrap. See KTPH006Local models with llama.cppKTPH007 and KTPH008RAG knowledge storesKTPH009.

Building from source requires a complete JDK and platform packaging tools. The dedicated guide covers the thin JAR, Java ZIP/TAR distributions, self-contained portable app images and native installers for every supported operating system, including Intel macOS builds, signing and notarization.

When launched via the Gradle daemon, korTTY runs as a child of a background process that has no Local Network permission, so connecting to LAN or private-IP hosts may fail. For LAN SSH, launch the packaged KTPH000, which prompts for Local Network access on first launch, or start korTTY as a child of Terminal.
